name: the war of Saryhorde and Keshband, 901
text: the war of Saryhorde and Keshband began in 901. The Saryhorde went to war with the Keshband as the Keshband first struck. The Keshband defeated the Saryhorde near Bortedag, 406 dead. Chuluun fell in battle. Bortedag was sacked by the Keshband. The Saryhorde was not without courage, but the Keshband was swift and strong. In 906, the Keshband again defeated the Saryhorde near Bortedag, 408 dead. Bortedag was sacked again. The Keshband was ever victorious, but the Saryhorde was ever ready. In 911, the Keshband defeated the Saryhorde once more, 411 dead. Bortedag was sacked a third time. Yet the Saryhorde and Keshband came to terms. The Keshband was strong, the Saryhorde was not. The Keshband was favored by Bayan the Unseen Weaver. The Saryhorde was not.

label: qwen3-4b
name: Winddiadem
text: Long ago, in the year 716, Bayan the Patient forged the Winddiadem of wrought iron at Silberscar. It passed to Gerel, then to Tsetseg, then to Yesui the Second, and finally to Chuluun. In 916, it was given to the temple of Bayan the Unseen Weaver at Karatau, but in 926, the Bortekhai carried it from Karaobo to Grafell. Now it is kept in the temple of Grafell, where it rests among the old stones and the wind that sings through the halls.

label: qwen3-4b
name: Farsignet
text: Long ago, in the year 776, Yesui the Second forged Farsignet of wrought iron at Bortedag. It was a ring of great power, shaped by the hands of a master smith. Soon after, it passed to Chuluun, who wore it with pride. Then it went to Gerel the Burned, who bore the weight of its legacy. Later, it was given to Temujin, who used it in his great endeavors. At last, in the year 921, Farsignet was laid in the tomb of Temujin, and now it rests in the barrow of Karaobo, where it waits for the day it may be found again.

label: qwen3-4b
name: Bayan the Unseen Weaver
text:
Trevanion the Unseen Weaver  
Bless us, Trevanion, with the thread of fate.  
We are the Boshold, and we walk the path of change.  
In Erzvein, we find the signs of your will.  
In Grimhold, the threads are woven tight.  
We bow to the Order of the Circle, ever loyal.  
The insect is our guide, and the sacred beast is ours.  
In Steingrube, we hear the whispers of the past.  
We are the keepers of the unseen weave.  
Bless us, Trevanion, and let the threads be true.
